text:
sam: FYI starting 01:10 UTC were seeing a burst of tiny-pod evictions in eu-central1. pending-tiny-pods jumped 120 -> 560 over 40m. Apps report intermittent out-of-memory retries and higher tail latency.

anya: any signs from node logs? maybe attach service errors or conntrack?

sam: grabbed logs from eu-nv-03 around 01:17:
```
Jan 09 01:17:05 kubelet[2890]: attach: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = websocket: close 1006
Jan 09 01:17:06 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
Jan 09 01:17:07 kubelet[2890]: attach: timeout waiting for device attach: context deadline exceeded
Jan 09 01:17:07 kubelet[2890]: evicting pod tiny-train-7d2 due to attach timeout
```

ben: looks like classic conntrack exhaustion + attach retries. But the scheduler is also scattering tiny pods due to rack-spread anti-affinity, which multiplies attach ops.

infra-bot: [alert] eu-central1: tiny-pod-evict-rate > 80/min (alert_id: infra:tiny-evict:3599).

zara: immediate mitigations: 1) apply scheduler soft-coalesce (pack small pods onto existing tiny nodes) 2) add attach-rate limiter in warmpool controller 3) canary bump nf_conntrack_max on select warm nodes.

ops-lead: prefer controller-side attach-rate limiter + scheduler hint. Bumping kernel params fleet-wide is last resort.

anya: i'll push a minimal scheduler scoring change as a canary: prefer nodes with tiny_count>0. PR: https://github.com/redwood/scheduler/pull/4332 (wip). Score algo: +100 if tiny_count>0, otherwise unchanged; respects tenant anti-affinity flags.

ben: i'll add a warmpool controller flag (ATTACH_RATE_LIMIT=10/s) and deploy to eu-central1-a canary. Also propose adding jitter (50-200ms) between attach attempts to smooth conn spikes.

sam: rollout plan: 1) deploy attach-rate-limiter to warmpool in eu-central1-a at 01:45 UTC 2) enable scheduler coalesce on 10 canary nodes (label canary=pack) 3) monitor 30m (metrics: pending-tiny-pods, evict-rate, attach-p95, nf_conntrack_count) 4) rollback if evict-rate not under 8/min or attach-p95 > 25s.

infra-bot: [update] canary started 01:47 UTC.

zara: note: coalescing can increase CPU contention on packed nodes; watch CPU steal and pod OOMs. But it reduces attach ops and cross-rack egress. cost tradeoff: denser packing usually cheaper than extra warm hosts.

ops-lead: document rollback steps and tag canary nodes with canary=attach-limiter for quick search. Also add alert to abort if node memory use grows > 75% after conntrack bump (if we end up doing that).

ben: initial canary metrics at 01:55 after 8m: pending-tiny-pods down 34%, evict-rate down 41%, attach-p95 down from 46s to 16s. early sign it's working.

anya: pushing scheduler PR to canary cluster now. keeping feature off by default; toggle via cluster feature-flag.

sam: thanks. keep monitoring for 30m. i'll update incident doc with PR links and rollback commands.

infra-bot: [final update] 30m window complete at 02:18 UTC: evict-rate=6.5/min (target <8), attach-p95=18.2s (target <25s), pending-tiny-pods stabilized. Rolling this to eu-central1 gradually and add telemetry to count avoided attach ops per tenant.

zara: follow-ups: 1) expose coalesce as per-namespace opt-in, 2) instrument attach-savings metric, 3) evaluate persistent attach proxy to reduce websocket churn.

ops-lead: good work. remember to include runbook steps and cost notes in the postmortem.

sam: will do. closing the loop. :white_check_mark:
